description: An inception with no traits, then a rotation whose configuration traits are [EO], signed by the exposed next key, then an interaction at sequence number 1 chained to the inception. EO may appear only in an inception (lines 367 and 371), and a validator must drop an event that breaks its traits' constraints (line 367), so it must drop the rotation. Nothing then makes the KEL establishment-only, and the interaction should be accepted on the inception's keys.

clauses.quote: A Validator of an event MUST invalidate, i.e., drop any events that do not satisfy the constraints imposed by their configuration traits.

dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-15; not yet raised with keripy or the KERI specification working group.
dispute.summary: keripy main reads configuration traits only from an identifier's inception (Kever.config is called when the Kever is created, never from Kever.update), so it accepts a rotation that carries EO, DND or DID as if its traits were empty, applies the rotation to the key state, and treats a later event at the rotation's sequence number as duplicitous.

title: Rotation carrying the establishment-only trait
